### Observed differences

- In the later window, A10 appears in about 70 in 100 traces (about 0.8 occurrences per trace), up from about 19 in 100 traces (about 0.2 occurrences) earlier. [OCC003]
- The routing around A14 changed: earlier, about 86 in 100 of A14's outgoing transitions went to A15 (with small shares to A08, A06, A02, A04) and almost none to A10; in the later window, about 66 in 100 go to A10 while about 33 still go directly to A15. A10's own outgoing, earlier spread across A46, A16, A48 and A21, now leads to A15 in about 85 in 100 cases. A14 is immediately followed by A10 in about 98 in 100 co-occurring later traces (133 traces versus 11 earlier), and A10 is followed by A15 within five steps in about 134 later traces (versus 3 earlier), usually at the next step. [DIR003, DIR002, LAG002, LAG001]
- A10's placement consolidated: earlier it sat at widely varying positions (mean about 0.55 of the trace, standard deviation 0.35); in the later window it occurs consistently early (mean about 0.19, standard deviation 0.15). A15 shifted slightly later (median about 0.16 to 0.18). [POS001, POS002]
- Two side activities receded: A08 appeared in about 20 in 100 traces earlier but only about 4 in 100 later; A04 fell from about 21 to about 11 in 100. A08's outgoing profile now rests on only 8 observed transitions (41 earlier). [OCC002, OCC001, DIR001]
- The middle block lost its fixed sequence. Earlier it ran as one chain, A31 → A22 → A20 → A23 → A24 → A26 → A25 → A32, with each pair in a single order in at least 96 in 100 co-occurring traces and at one short lag. In the later window many pairs run in both orders: A23 precedes A24 in only about 15 in 100 (A24 first in about 85; earlier it was 98 the other way); A20 precedes A24 in about 25 (earlier 99); A23 precedes A26 in about 32 (earlier 97); A20/A26, A23/A25 and A22/A24 now occur in each order about half the time. New transitions appeared, such as A23 → A32 (about 47 of A23's outgoing), A24 → A22 (about 23), A22 → A24 (about 27), A25 → A20 (about 20) and A31 → A24 (about 46). Gaps between consecutive activities spread from a single value to one to five steps (for example A24 → A26 at lag 1 in about 61 in 100 later versus 99 earlier). [REL020, REL015, REL022, REL017, REL021, REL018, REL019, REL016, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR009, DIR010, LAG018, LAG013, LAG016, LAG028, LAG022, LAG020]
- Positions in that block shifted mildly (A20, A22, A23 later by about 0.03–0.06 of trace length; A24, A25, A26 earlier by about 0.01–0.05), and the closing segment became more rigid: A45 → A46 and A47 → A48 are now almost always adjacent (lag 1 in about 58 and 99 in 100 cases, up from about 47 and 87). [POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, DIR011, LAG030, LAG032]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

Screening qualified 77 control-flow items against roughly 1 expected if nothing had changed, so the flagged differences as a whole are unlikely to be sampling noise. The evidence supports the possibility that work on the path between A14 and A15, which earlier passed directly from A14 to A15 in most cases, now typically passes through A10 (A14 → A10 → A15), turning A10 from a rare, variably placed activity (about 19 in 100 traces, mean position about 0.55) into a frequent, early, consistently placed step (about 70 in 100 traces, position about 0.19, immediately after A14 and leading to A15). The successor changes at A14 and A10 are direct relational evidence, and the occurrence, position and lag indicators agree across 200 traces per window; the many relation items pairing A10 with other activities largely restate the same participation change and are not independent confirmations. Limitations: A10 occurs in only about 70 of 100 later traces, so the evidence cannot tell whether the step is optional or taken only in part of the caseload, nor whether the decline of A08 (about 20 to 4 in 100 traces) and A04 (about 21 to 11) belongs to the same restructuring. A competing explanation that cannot be ruled out is that the later window mixes traces with and without the new A10 step rather than one uniformly modified flow. [OCC003, DIR003, DIR002, LAG002, LAG001, POS001, OCC002, OCC001]

Other differences: the block A20, A22, A23, A24, A25 and A26 changed from a fixed chain into a flexible, repetition-prone block — pairs that earlier had one order and lag now occur in both orders with one-to-five-step gaps, and new transitions such as A23 → A32, A24 → A22, A25 → A20 and A31 → A24 carry substantial shares; this is a change in ordering constraints rather than a swap of positions, and while it may be part of the same restructuring, the evidence does not link it to the A10 change. [REL020, REL015, REL022, REL017, REL021, REL018, DIR006, DIR007, DIR008, DIR010, LAG018, LAG013, LAG016, LAG028, DIR011]
